lead: A module is one .py file that other code imports by name. A package is a folder of modules with an __init__.py file, so Python treats the folder as one importable unit. This arrangement lets you split a long program into small files, reuse code, and borrow from Python's standard library. Every import follows the same path: check the cache, search sys.path, run the file once, bind a name. Indian exams often ask for the search order, the __name__ guard, and a dotted import such as shop.billing.
prereq: You need 5.5 for sys.path, Unit 2 for functions, and Unit 4 for grouping code into classes and modules.

sections.h3: Module, import, and the search path

blocks.text: A module is one .py file. A package is a folder with an __init__.py file and one or more module files. The folder becomes one importable unit. Python has four common import forms. import mymath binds the name mymath; use mymath.square(7). from mymath import PI binds only PI. import shop.billing binds shop; call shop.billing.gst(1000). import mymath as m binds m. from mymath import * binds all public names; avoid it in exam answers because the bound names are unclear.

An import does five things. First, Python checks sys.modules, a cache of modules already imported. If the name is there, it binds the name and stops. Second, it checks built-in modules such as sys. Third, it searches the folders listed in sys.path. The first entry is the script's folder, so a local file can hide a standard module. Fourth, for a package it runs shop/__init__.py, then runs billing.py once. Fifth, it binds the dotted name shop.billing in the importing file.

sections.h3: Write a module, guard it, make a package

blocks.text: Your own module. Put code in mymath.py in the same folder as the script. The file can hold PI = 3.14159 and def square(n): return n * n. A second file uses import mymath. Top-level code in a module runs at the first import and not again. A counter at module level keeps its old value on the next import.
The guard. A file may be run directly or imported. __name__ is '__main__' when run directly and the module name when imported. The guard keeps test code out of imports.

Package. Make a folder shop. Add an empty shop/__init__.py. Add shop/billing.py with def gst(amount): return amount * 0.18. The empty __init__.py marks the folder as a package. Then import shop.billing works if shop is on sys.path. Python runs shop/__init__.py first, then billing.py once. Call shop.billing.gst(1000) to get 180.0 rupees. from shop import billing binds billing directly.

sections.h3: Exploring modules and the standard library

blocks.text: Use dir(module) to list names inside a module. dir() with no argument lists names in the current scope. Use help(module) to read the docstring and function signatures. These two tools save exam time when you forget a function name.

head: Module
Use
rows: sqrt, pi, ceil for numeric work
randint, choice, seed for tests and games
getcwd, listdir, path.join for folders and paths
argv, path, version for interpreter state
search, findall, sub for patterns; full use in 5.7

blocks.text: Import only what you need in small programs: from math import sqrt, pi. In larger programs, import math is clearer because math.sqrt shows the source. Keep module names short and lowercase. Do not name a file random.py or math.py.

figure.caption: The flow checks the cache first and binds at once if the name is there; otherwise it searches the folders in sys.path, runs the package marker, then the module file once.

spec.title: What import does
spec.aria: An import first checks the sys.modules cache and binds the name at once if found, otherwise searches the folders in sys.path, runs the package __init__.py, runs the module file once and binds the dotted name.

examples.question: mymath.py holds PI = 3.14159 and def square(n): return n * n. A second file uses it, then uses a package shop/billing.py whose gst(amount) returns amount * 0.18. Give the values of mymath.square(7), PI after from mymath import PI, and shop.billing.gst(1000).
steps: from mymath import PI binds PI to the value 3.14159.
shop/__init__.py is empty; it only marks shop/ as a package, and import runs it before billing.py.

traps: A file named random.py or math.py in the working folder hides the standard module, because sys.path starts with the script folder.
Top-level code runs once at the first import, not on every import. A module-level counter keeps its old value.
import shop.billing binds shop, not billing. Write shop.billing.gst(...), or use from shop import billing.
__init__.py may be empty, but it must exist for a regular package in exam answers; it runs before any submodule.
from mymath import PI copies the binding at import time. If mymath.PI changes later, the imported PI does not change.

quiz.q: Define module and package in one line each.
quiz.a: A module is one .py file imported by name. A package is a folder with __init__.py and modules, imported as one unit.

quiz.q: Why does a module use if __name__ == '__main__'?
quiz.a: Top-level code runs on import. The guard runs test code only when the file is run directly, not when imported.

quiz.q: mymath.py has PI = 3.14159 and square(n) = n * n. What does this print? import mymath; print(mymath.square(5)); print(mymath.PI)
quiz.a: 25 then 3.14159, each on its own line.

quiz.q: A folder has random.py and a script. The script says import random. Which file is used and why?
quiz.a: Local random.py is used because sys.path starts with the script folder; it hides the standard random module.

quiz.q: shop/__init__.py is empty and shop/billing.py defines gst(amount) = amount * 0.18. Write the call for 2000 rupees and give the result.
A module prints 'loaded' at top level. A program imports it twice with import mymod. How many times does 'loaded' print and why?
quiz.a: Once. The first import runs the file and stores it in sys.modules; the second import finds the cache and binds the name.

quiz.q: Name two standard library modules and one use of each.
quiz.a: math for sqrt and pi; random for randint and choice.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real projects install third-party packages with pip and record them in pyproject.toml or requirements.txt. Python also has namespace packages, where a folder can be a package without __init__.py in some versions, and importlib lets code import at runtime. Virtual environments keep project packages separate. Search for Python packaging user guide, venv and importlib to go further.
